findings.evidence: The record's own measured_run.breakage_output does not match its expected_failure text, and re-running the documented breakage confirms this independently. expected_failure claims: "The edge adapter, with no guard before assuming the wire body is a well-formed dict, crashes with a traceback (AttributeError)... the in-process adapter is unaffected and still passes." Following the breakage field exactly (edit harness/errors/adapters/second.py to remove the media-type/registered-type guard in classify(), then run `bash harness/errors/test.sh && python3 harness/errors/conformance.py --adapter dryrun --adapter second`) instead produces: section 1 (dry-run adapter) FAILs, section 2 (swap proof) FAILs, and section 4 ends with `AssertionError: the breakage pattern was not found; test.sh is out of sync with second.py` -- not an AttributeError, and the in-process (dryrun) adapter does NOT still pass. I reproduced this exactly: `passed 17, failed 6` with the identical traceback, matching the record's own stored breakage_output verbatim. The cause: test.sh's own section 4 applies the identical patch internally (to a copy under out/breakage/); once a caller has already hand-edited second.py per the breakage instructions, test.sh's internal string-replace no longer finds its target and the harness's self-check throws, corrupting the very run the criterion asks the reader to perform.
findings.fix: Rewrite the breakage/expected_failure text to instruct running only `python3 conformance.py --adapter second` on a hand-edited copy (as test.sh's own section 4 already does internally), or change the DoD criterion so the documented manual breakage does not collide with test.sh's built-in auto-breakage step.

summary: Read OWNER.md, docs/acceptance/ceremony.json, .claude/skills/build-ceremony/SKILL.md and kb/ceremonies/59-build-review-a.json for shape and depth, then reviewed all 13 STATUS-row-60 skills row by row against their skill.json data, without reading any kb/ceremonies/60-* file. Ran python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <name> for each of the 13 skills (all report 0 errors; warning counts ranged 1-9, mostly the restate-and-extend and restate-under-same-quote checks) and used those runs, plus python3 tools/kb.py show on every distinct cited id I spot-checked (all sourced quotes I checked, including every numeric/specific claim in cap-agent-runtime, cap-capability-packaging, cap-capability-registry and cap-durable-execution, verified as verbatim substrings that do support the row's claim), to find findings. Ran every 'measured' definition_of_done once: harness/containment (cap-agent-runtime-implement), harness/capability-packaging, harness/capability-registry (clean and breakage both run twice due to a sandboxed retry), harness/document-validation, harness/workflow (cap-durable-execution-implement, breakage exercised internally by test.sh), harness/errors, and examples/end-to-end/test.sh (cap-consumption) -- 13 runs total, tree left clean after each (git status confirmed empty). Six of the seven reproduced their recorded clean and breakage output exactly. Two did not: cap-errors-implement's documented breakage recipe, followed exactly as written, does not produce its documented expected_failure -- it instead reproduces an internal harness self-check error already sitting (unnoticed) in the record's own measured_run.breakage_output (R60A-001, high). cap-consumption's clean-run expected text ('passed 29, failed 0') is stale against the suite's current count of 30 (R60A-002, low; the criterion itself still passes and the breakage half reproduced exactly). No fabricated quotes were found (no case where a quote was a verbatim substring of a cited record but the record did not support the row's claim, in the style of the ceremony-59 example) among the rows checked; validate_skills.py's own verbatim-substring check reported 0 errors on all 13 skills, meaning no cited quote failed that check outright. No uncited non-proposed claims (0 errors on that check either). No adapters[] row named a product outside the designated adapters section, and every second adapter differs from its 'today' adapter on a genuine execution-model axis I could verify from its binding schema and swap_procedure text (agent-runtime: session vs single-shot; capability-packaging: directory vs registry; capability-registry: signed local index vs network fetch; document-validation: in-process walk-per-doc vs out-of-process compile-once; durable-execution: external replay orchestrator vs in-process transactional step log; errors: in-process factory vs edge wire-filter) -- cap-durable-execution and cap-durable-execution-implement name real products (Temporal, DBOS) but only inside adapters[], which is where agentic-stack's own rule says products belong. No description trigger clause across the 13 skills failed to fire on its own stated scope. No proposed row read as padding or as a reword of a sibling row in the same skill. The remaining findings (R60A-003 through R60A-014, all low severity) are the restatement pattern already named in build-ceremony's own author-brief lesson: a sourced row in 12 of the 13 skills restates a fact agentic-stack, build-adapter-pair, build-definition-of-done, build-evidence-record, build-ceremony, or a sibling cap- skill already states under the identical quote, either without naming that owner or by extending the restatement with an unmarked, uncited consequence clause after an 'already states / what it adds' marker. cap-consumption was the one skill in this batch with no restatement finding.
